A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDLG research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison; the rotated appendix table is readable.

before.justification: V1 reports original uncertainty-estimation experiments on TruthfulQA, CoQA, and TriviaQA, computational and semantic-cluster analyses, and a synthetic estimator simulation.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds an experiment ablating SDLG's token scores in Appendix E, Figure 9.

M1.justification: The token scores, ranking procedure, token substitution and continuation, and entropy estimators remain unchanged. The restriction to substituting word-initial tokens in v2 Section 4 was already stated in v1 Section 6; its relocation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TruthfulQA, CoQA, and TriviaQA question-answering coverage and synthetic cluster-distribution example. The new ablation uses existing TruthfulQA coverage rather than introducing another task, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparison methods. However, the CoQA sample-count comparison in v2 Figure 3(a), corresponding to v1 Figure 7(a), removes PE, LN-PE, and SAR curves while retaining SDLG and multinomial-sampling variants. Newly cited methods such as EigenScore are not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 Figure 9 introduces a controlled comparison of score subsets on OPT-2.7b and TruthfulQA: importance is always included, and included scores receive equal weights. Existing benchmark splits, prompts, model sizes, correctness metrics and thresholds, generation counts, and baseline hyperparameter searches are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused ablation testing the separate contributions of attribution and substitution scores alongside importance. The estimator simulation, threshold sensitivity, semantic-cluster analysis, computational analysis, and generated-answer examples already existed in v1; moving or explaining them further does not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report bias and variance over 200 runs for the same synthetic simulation in Appendix C. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the question-answering experiments or new ablation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all three correctness-threshold/sample-count heatmaps retain their numerical results. V2 adds ablation curves showing generally strongest performance with all scores and a larger contribution from substitution than attribution. It also removes the PE, LN-PE, and SAR sample-count curves from the matched CoQA comparison.

T1.justification: Equations 1–21, the uncertainty decomposition, entropy estimators, and Appendix B proposal-distribution derivation are retained. The strong assumption concentrating substitution-position probability at the observed position is unchanged; no new proof or mathematical correction is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same two principal contributions: semantically diverse generation for improved uncertainty estimation and a theoretical foundation for semantic-entropy estimation. Claims concerning question-answering performance and sampling/computational efficiency retain their substantive scope; v2's revised hallucination framing does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the causal framing of hallucinations, introduces confabulation terminology, and adds interpretations of dataset differences and score contributions. It removes v1's explicit discussion of untested longer tasks, difficulty assessing their correctness, and conditioning semantic diversity only on the first output. Hard-cluster and epistemic-uncertainty limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 omits v1's five-beam initial-generation and shared-first-output description, four A100 80GB GPU disclosure, and under-1000-GPU-hour estimate. Core hyperparameters and the Appendix D code/data link remain. A new reproducibility statement promises code upon publication, but the PDFs do not establish an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Bakman, Chen, Farquhar, and Nikitin and a complementary-methods paragraph positioning SDLG as potentially useful for Lin's similarity-based estimator and Chen's EigenScore. This updates the research context without replacing the existing positioning or experimentally comparing those additional methods.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, expands evaluation and computational-flow explanations, revises the conclusion, and adds an ethics and reproducibility statement. Hyperparameter details move to Appendix D. These are localized narrative revisions within the retained seven main sections and Appendices A–E.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: existing CoQA performance/cluster and computational-cost plots move into the main text, Figure 1 is redesigned, and a new ablation figure is added. The CoQA plot has reduced comparator legends and rescaled axes, while appendix figures and Table 2 are rearranged within the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: V2 adds direct evidence for individual score contributions through the previously absent ablation and makes evaluation and computational flow easier to understand. Bringing efficiency evidence into the main text also improves assessability. These modest gains are tempered by lost initial-generation and hardware details and removed limitations; the core theory and benchmark results remain unchanged.
